name: Rocky Knob

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. It is very acid, which locks up nutrients, so growers spread lime to raise the pH.

land: The high ground runs about 5°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
